name: Veres
title: The Watching Wing
description: A dark-winged angel who has watched this island longer than the Saints have been building on it. She chose the mountain. She does not regret this.

dialogue: Most people who find me up here don't try to fight me. Interesting choice.
Come back when you want to talk instead.
You've earned a conversation, at least.

swordRanks.title: The Watcher on the Mountain
swordRanks.description: There is an angel on the central mountain who has been watching this island for longer than most things on it have been alive. She seems willing to talk.

unavailable_dialogue: I'm not annoyed. I expected it eventually.
Come back when you're ready to actually talk.
intro_dialogue: Either you're good at looking, or the mountain wanted you here.
I've learned not to argue with the mountain.
success_dialogue: I've been up here long enough to know when something changes in the air below.
The Towers. The Saints. The particular quality of violence spreading across Ashenfall.
I watch. I remember. I don't intervene — not yet.
Hela sent you, didn't she.
Don't bother denying it. I've known her for centuries. She has exactly one method of reaching out, and it's sending someone interesting ahead of herself.
She's well?
Good. She worries me sometimes. The ones who carry the most tend to make it look easiest.
You should come back. I find I want to know what you make of things.
Oh — and what do you think of the hair? I changed it recently.
I do that. It helps me remember I'm still in motion, even when I'm sitting still.

swordRanks.title: Something in the Air
swordRanks.description: Veres has noticed a change in the Biceons — the ice bisons of the central mountain. They have been restless. She wants to know why.

unavailable_dialogue: Something is wrong with the Biceons. I can feel it in the wind off the mountain.
Come back soon. I don't like what I'm hearing.
intro_dialogue: I have a problem I'd like your help with.
success_dialogue: The Biceons. You may have seen them — ice bisons, central mountain, impossible to miss.
We have an understanding, the Biceons and I. Have had, for decades.
They tolerate my presence on their mountain. I keep the worst weather off their grazing ground in winter. It works.
Three weeks ago they stopped coming near my post. Yesterday, two charged a path they've walked peacefully for years.
Something is agitating them. I need to know what.
Go onto the mountain. Find them. One will be aggressive — it happens when they're frightened.
Deal with it if you have to. I trust your judgement on what 'deal with it' means.
Then come back to me.

reminder_dialogue: The mountain. The Biceons are up there.
Be careful — they're not malicious. They're scared. That makes them more dangerous, not less.
success_dialogue: You handled it.
Come. Sit. Tell me what you found.

swordRanks.title: What the Wind Carries
swordRanks.description: Veres has been listening to the wind. Something near the Tower construction is pushing the Biceons off their range. She wants to understand it better.

unavailable_dialogue: I'm still listening. Come back shortly.
intro_dialogue: I've been thinking about what you reported.
The Biceons don't frighten easily. Whatever is doing this has been building for a while.
success_dialogue: I've been listening to the wind since you left. Really listening.
There's a frequency coming off the Tower construction to the south. Not sound — something underneath sound.
The Biceons feel it. Their sense of the mountain's resonance is older and finer than mine.
When the Towers go up, the island's natural flow shifts. The Biceons are living instruments for that kind of disturbance.
I've seen this island change before. Slowly. The way things that are meant to change do.
This is not that.
I want you to go to the southern edge of the mountain range — the closest point to the Tower site.
There's a place the Biceons used to graze. I need to know if they're still going there.
Look for tracks. Look for what's missing.
I'll be here. Working something out.

reminder_dialogue: Southern edge of the mountain range. Look for the flat expanse below the snowline.
You'll know it by the silence. Nothing grazes there anymore.
success_dialogue: Empty.
I thought so.
They haven't been there in weeks. The ground confirms it.
This is the Tower's doing. Not malice — I don't think whoever is building them even knows.
But it doesn't matter whether they know. The result is the same.
Thank you. I needed to be certain before I said it out loud.
Come back. I want to keep talking to you.
Oh — different hair again. Do you notice? I got bored. This is what centuries does to you.
You stop worrying about consistency and start worrying about whether you're still curious.

swordRanks.title: Old Debt
swordRanks.description: Veres has something she wants to say. About the Saints. About Guinevere. About why she watches and does not act.

unavailable_dialogue: I'm not ready yet. Give me a little time.
Some things need to be said in the right moment.
success_dialogue: Can I tell you something I haven't said to anyone up here?
I know Guinevere.
Not from reports. Not from watching the Cathedral from above.
I knew her before she was Commander. Before she was even very much a soldier.
She was— she had this quality. Of absolute belief in what she was doing.
Not arrogance. Conviction. There's a difference, and she knew the difference.
We were close. For a time. The kind of close that the Saints would have had opinions about.
She made her choice. I made mine.
I don't regret it. I don't think she does either.
What I regret is watching what that belief became.
She still does good. Every day, genuinely, she does good.
And the Towers are going up.
I watch because I owe her the respect of witnessing what she's built.
I don't act because I owe her the same.
But the Biceons are off their range.
And something in me is running out of reasons to stay still.
You should know that. Since you're the one I've been telling everything to.
I don't know why I trust you so easily.
Actually — I do. Hela sent you. And Hela only sends people she's decided matter.
That's a better reference than most.

swordRanks.title: The Wind Decides
swordRanks.description: Veres has made a decision. She won't say what it is yet — but she's done watching.

unavailable_dialogue: I'm almost ready. The wind is still settling.
success_dialogue: I've been up here for eleven years.
That's not very long, for me. But it's long enough.
I came here because I was finished with the world being loud.
The world has gotten loud again.
The Biceons don't deserve what the Towers are doing to their home. The island doesn't deserve it.
And I think — I think I have been using 'neutrality' as a word for 'afraid to care again'.
I'm done with that.
I'm not siding with anyone yet. I want to be clear about that.
But I am going to come down from the mountain.
Hela will be insufferably pleased about this.
Tell her I said she was right, and then refuse to repeat it if she asks.
You — you've been good to talk to.
Better than I expected from someone Hela described as 'quietly catastrophic'.
That's the highest thing she says about anyone, you know.
Take care of yourself out there.
And come back. There's more to say, when there's time to say it properly.
The mountain will be here.

rank_up_dialogue: You keep finding your way back up here.
I've been on this mountain long enough to know that most people don't bother twice.
You're different. I noticed.
I appreciate it more than I'll probably say directly.
The hair, by the way — what do you think of this one? I was going for something softer.
I change it when I'm thinking. Which means it changes a lot.

dialogue: The last person who brought me Forza Mead ended up telling me their entire life story.
I don't mind. I have time.
What exactly is your plan here.
Fine. They're actually very good. Don't look at me like that.
I've been alone on a mountain for eleven years. This is very welcome.

rank_up_dialogue: I don't do this lightly.
Trust. Letting someone close enough that what they think of me starts to matter.
I've had centuries of practice at keeping a certain distance.
You managed to be interesting enough that I forgot to maintain it.
I'm not complaining.
Just — be careful with it. That's all I'll say.

dialogue: I like that you pay attention to small things.
I'm starting to think this is less of a gift and more of a hint.
The mountain gets cold at night. There are worse reasons to visit.
I find I'm running low on it, around you.
Make of that what you will.
You know, the last time I drank this much Forza Mead I made some very questionable decisions.

rank_up_dialogue: You know what I haven't done in a very long time?
Let someone see the version of me that existed before the mountain.
I was — I was a lot, back then. Loud. Reckless. I loved people the way weather loves coasts.
Completely. Destructively. With zero interest in being reasonable about it.
I have galleries of that version. Paintings, mostly. I look at them and feel very fond of her.
She didn't know what she was doing.
Neither do I, honestly.
But I think that's alright, now.
Don't go anywhere.

dialogue: The mountain is very private, you know.
Tell me something I don't know yet.
I have centuries of things to trade.
